author: Gmelin, 1789
summary: 하구, 저수지, 호수 등에 찾아오는 매우 드문 겨울철새로, 물풀의 뿌리와 줄기를 먹는다. 전국에 찾아오지만 호수 주변 개발과 수초 제거 등으로 찾아오는 수가 줄고 있다. 유럽 중·서부, 몽골, 바이칼호 동부, 우수리강 유역에서 번식하고 소아시아, 북아프리카, 중국 동부, 한국에서 겨울을 난다.

points.en: black knob at the base of the bill

art.subject: Mute Swan (Cygnus olor), adult in winter (sexes alike, the male with a larger knob): entire plumage pure white, the head sometimes faintly stained rusty from feeding; bill orange-red with a black nail, black base and black lores, and a prominent black knob at the base of the upper mandible over the forehead; dark eye set in the black facial skin; black legs and feet.
art.pose: swimming on calm water, reaching down to feed on water plants
art.scene: calm Korean reservoir in winter with open water and aquatic plants; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view swimming: all-white plumage, neck in an S-curve, orange bill with a black knob and black base, pointed tail raised, wings slightly arched
adult, head close-up in profile: orange-red bill with a black nail, black lores and base, and a prominent black knob above the bill base
adult standing on the bank, side view: all-white body held horizontally, short black legs set far back, large black webbed feet, neck gently curved
art.build: Very large, heavy swan, 152cm, larger than Whooper Swan (Cygnus cygnus), with a long, thick neck usually held in a graceful S-curve while swimming, the bill pointing downward. Pointed tail often raised. Often swims with the wings arched up over the back. Legs black, short, set far back. In flight the long neck is stretched straight forward.
avoid: Do not paint yellow on the bill — yellow-and-black bills belong to Whooper Swan (Cygnus cygnus) and Tundra Swan (Cygnus columbianus).
Do not omit the black knob at the bill base.
Do not hold the neck stiffly straight and upright like Whooper Swan; the Mute Swan usually curves it.
Do not paint orange or pink legs; they are black.
